hero_kpi_rationale: Falcon launches are the group's flagship product and its most distinctive metric: the only KPI on the page with ten years of history, from 8 launches in 2016 to 165 in 2025.

kpis.name: Falcon Launches
kpis.explanation: Successful Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy flights per calendar year, customer missions and internal Starlink deployments combined.
kpis.description: The company's flagship product. Figures for 2023 to 2025 come from the company report; earlier years come from the public reference count of Falcon launches.
kpis.signal: 165 Falcon launches in 2025 versus 134 in 2024 and 8 in 2016: cadence has risen twentyfold in ten years. 106 launches had been flown by 10 September 2026.

kpis.name: Total Launches
kpis.explanation: All successful orbital launches and flight tests of the year, Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy and Starship included.
kpis.description: Operational scale metric published by the company, internal deployments included.
kpis.signal: 170 launches in 2025, of which 165 Falcon and 5 Starship flights.

kpis.name: Starlink Subscribers
kpis.explanation: Active Starlink service lines at year end, consumer and business plans, excluding negotiated enterprise and government contracts.
kpis.description: A service line is one Starlink subscription tied to a Starlink.com account. A household may hold several.
kpis.signal: 8.9 million subscribers at the end of 2025 versus 4.4 million a year earlier, and 12.0 million at 30 June 2026.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Annual consolidated revenue across the Space, Connectivity and AI segments.
kpis.description: Prior years are recast to include xAI and X, acquired under common control.
kpis.signal: $18,674 million in 2025, up 33.2% after 34.9% in 2024, driven mainly by Starlink.

kpis.name: Connectivity Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue of the Connectivity segment: Starlink consumer, enterprise, government and mobility offerings.
kpis.description: Consumer $7,208 million and enterprise and government $4,179 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: $11,387 million in 2025 versus $3,869 million in 2023: Starlink is now the group's largest business, at 61% of consolidated revenue.

kpis.name: Space Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue of the Space segment: launch services for external customers and development contracts for space agencies.
kpis.description: Internal launches generate no inter-segment revenue and are therefore excluded.
kpis.signal: $4,086 million in 2025, up only 7.6%: launch capacity is absorbed by internal Starlink deployments.

kpis.name: AI Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue of the AI segment: advertising on X, Grok subscriptions, AI solutions and compute infrastructure.
kpis.description: Advertising $1,844 million and AI solutions and infrastructure $1,357 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: $3,201 million in 2025: advertising has fallen since 2023 while AI solutions and infrastructure more than doubled.

kpis.name: Starlink Subscriber ARPU
kpis.explanation: Starlink service revenue divided by the average number of subscribers and by the number of months in the period.
kpis.description: The company expects ARPU to keep declining as international expansion continues.
kpis.signal: $81 per month in 2025 versus $99 in 2023: the company prioritises volume over price.

kpis.name: Mass to Orbit
kpis.explanation: Total payload mass deployed to orbit during the year, Starlink satellites, customer payloads and development cargo included.
kpis.description: A Falcon 9 carries 13 metric tons per mission on average since 2023.
kpis.signal: 2,213 metric tons to orbit in 2025, of which 1,901 for internal payloads.

kpis.name: Internal Falcon Launches
kpis.explanation: Falcon launches whose primary payload belongs to the group, mostly Starlink satellites.
kpis.description: All Starship flights are classified as internal to date.
kpis.signal: 122 internal launches out of 165 in 2025: three quarters of capacity builds the company's own constellation.

kpis.name: Customer Falcon Launches
kpis.explanation: Falcon launches whose primary payload belongs to an external customer and whose mission profile is designed around it.
kpis.description: Billable base of the Space segment.
kpis.signal: 43 customer launches in 2025 versus 45 in 2024, while total cadence rose by 31.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Annual capital expenditure across all segments.
kpis.description: AI $12,727 million, Connectivity $4,178 million and Space $3,832 million in 2025.

kpis.name: Research and Development
kpis.description: Expensed research and development, before capitalisation.
kpis.signal: $8,643 million in 2025, or 46% of revenue, driven by Starship and the Grok models.

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Consolidated operating result for the year.
kpis.description: By segment in 2025: Connectivity $4,423 million, Space -$657 million, AI -$6,355 million.
kpis.signal: Operating loss of $2,589 million in 2025 after a $466 million profit in 2024.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Consolidated net result for the year.
kpis.description: The 2023 loss includes $3,775 million of impairment related to X.
kpis.signal: Net loss of $4,937 million in 2025, with $1,945 million of interest expense on top of the operating loss.

kpis.name: Nameplate Compute Draw
kpis.explanation: Nameplate electrical draw of the group's AI data centres at period end.
kpis.description: Capacity metric published by the company for the AI segment.
kpis.signal: 0.8 gigawatt installed at the end of 2025 versus 0.3 a year earlier, and 1.4 gigawatt at 30 June 2026.

kpis.name: Connectivity Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA of the Connectivity segment.
kpis.description: Non-GAAP measure published by the company and reconciled to segment operating income.
kpis.signal: $7,168 million in 2025, 63% of segment revenue: Starlink funds the rest of the group.

kpis.name: Cash from Operations
kpis.explanation: Net cash generated by operating activities during the year.
kpis.description: From the consolidated statement of cash flows.
kpis.signal: $6,785 million generated in 2025, three times less than the $20,737 million invested.

risks.title: Any delay in scaling Starship would block the growth strategy
risks.description: The company report lists first the risk that Starship fails to reach scale, cadence, reusability and capability. Only twelve flight tests have been flown to date and none has been classified as a customer mission, yet next-generation Starlink satellites, direct-to-mobile connectivity and orbital AI compute all depend on it.

risks.title: Loss or delay of launch and re-entry licences from the U.S. aviation regulator
risks.description: Space activities depend on launch and re-entry licences. The company report states that any delay or difficulty in obtaining, maintaining or renewing them would materially delay or disrupt operations.

risks.title: Dependence on communications licences and spectrum authorisations
risks.description: Satellite connectivity relies on national and international spectrum licences, on international telecommunication rules and on country-by-country coordination, including the S-band spectrum acquired from EchoStar.

risks.title: Dependence on U.S. federal agencies, with one customer above one fifth of revenue
risks.description: One customer accounted for 20.9% of consolidated revenue in 2025, after 24.2% in 2024 and 25.2% in 2023. About one fifth of revenue comes from U.S. federal agencies.

risks.title: Investment pace above internally generated cash
risks.description: The company invested $20,737 million in 2025 while generating $6,785 million of operating cash. The company report warns that insufficient cash generation or financing would have a material adverse effect.

risks.title: High level of indebtedness
risks.description: Interest expense reached $1,945 million in 2025, more than the operating loss of the year.

risks.title: Launch failures, the space environment and orbital debris
risks.description: Launch delays and failures have occurred and will occur again. Satellites and vehicles operate in a harsh environment, and the proliferation of constellations and debris may limit deployment.

risks.title: Founder control and multiple voting rights
risks.description: The founder is chief executive, chief technical officer and chairman, and holds 84.4% of combined voting power after the offering. Class B shares carry ten votes and elect a majority of the board.

governance.notes: Elon Musk is chief executive officer, chief technical officer and chairman of the board, and holds 84.4% of combined voting power after the offering. Class A shares carry one vote, Class B shares ten votes, and Class B holders elect 51% of the board. Five of the eight directors are independent under Nasdaq rules. The chief executive received only his $54,080 base salary in 2025 and no equity award; the president and chief operating officer received $85.8 million, mostly in options.

ai_positioning.summary: Artificial intelligence is one of the group's three businesses, not a side use. The AI segment, formed from xAI and X, generated $3,201 million of revenue in 2025 and $2,561 million in the quarter ended 30 June 2026 alone. Installed compute rose from 0.3 gigawatt at the end of 2024 to 1.4 gigawatt at 30 June 2026. The cost is visible: $12,727 million invested in AI in 2025 and a segment operating loss of $6,355 million.
evidence: Dedicated AI segment: $3,201 million of revenue in 2025, of which $1,844 million advertising and $1,357 million AI solutions and infrastructure.
AI segment capital expenditure of $12,727 million in 2025 versus $5,633 million in 2024 and $463 million in 2023.
Installed compute draw raised from 0.3 gigawatt at end-2024 to 0.8 gigawatt at end-2025 and 1.4 gigawatt at 30 June 2026.
The AI segment turned adjusted EBITDA positive for the first time in the quarter ended 30 June 2026, at $1.1 billion, after -$1,237 million in 2025.
The group is developing orbital compute capacity, a direct extension of its launchers and constellation.
Acknowledged trade-off: the AI segment lost $6,355 million at the operating level in 2025, more than Connectivity earned.
ai_positioning.source: Company report: initial public offering prospectus of 12 June 2026 and quarterly report of 4 August 2026
